chapter: Long Branch and the war years
title: The 1942 walk-a-thon bands at Turner's Arena and 26th Street
summary: Back in D.C., Phillips played Tex Briscoe's eight-piece band for a summer-long walk-a-thon with Fats Wright, Osie Johnson and John Malachi, moving to a second one on 26th Street until November 1942.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: After that time, you came back to D.C., right?
You started working with Coridge [DUPRE'S SPELLING] Davis in '45.
But anything you want to mention before that -- from Labor Day of '41 on til '45?

After I came back from Asbury Park, they had a walk-a-thon here. Up there at Turner's Arena. I don't know if you remember that or not. That's between 14th and 13th on W Street. That was a big place where all the bands used to come, good shows -- big arena. They had a walk-a-thon there for the whole summer. Tex Briscoe got the job up there. We had Fats Wright. Did you ever hear of him? Piano player. Helluva piano player. He's dead now. His name was Clyde Wright. He died about a couple of years ago.
So he was on this gig with you and Briscoe?
Up there. He was playing piano at Turner's Arena. Osie Johnson was playing drums. Julius Pogue was

playing tenor. A cat we called Cragbrains -- Cragbrains Page -- was playing tenor. Then Butch Hamilton was playing alto. Then we had Wash -- Milton Washington -- playing trumpet. And I was playing trumpet. So we had eight pieces. I stayed up there until that one closed. Then they opened up again, out there somewhere where Charlie's is, 26th Street -- somewhere out there.
It used to be a big thing here...
That's the Walk-A-Thon. We're still at the Walk-a-Thon. The one up there at Turner's Arena, when that one closed, they moved out on 26th Street...

That was all of '42, practically. We went up to this Walk-a-Thon... They stayed about six months, you know. It opened up in June, and we left this one in August, and we went to the one out there and stayed until November. When that was over, John got a gig... John was playing with us on this Walk-A-Thon, too -- on that one out on 26th Street.
So that's the second time you played with John. You played with him in Tommy Miles' band and then played with him in '42?
Yeah. That was the second time.
